Words in context questions ask which word fits a blank. The right answer isn't the fanciest word. It's the word the text's clue points to.
Here's the method. Cover the choices. Find the clue. Say your own simple word in the blank. Then pick the choice closest to your word.
Try this one. Foreign problems led to blank within Russia. For instance, protests broke out.
The clue is, protests broke out. My own word is trouble. So the answer is unrest.
Clues come in a few flavors. A colon explains what came before it. Whereas and unlike flip to the opposite. And an effect tells you the cause.
Here's an unlike clue. Unlike her outspoken colleagues, the physicist was blank, rarely speaking to reporters.
Unlike means opposite. The opposite of outspoken is quiet. So the answer is reserved.
Trap alert. Boastful matches outspoken. That's the same as the clue, but unlike needs the opposite.
Now an effect clue. The new evidence blank the old theory. Researchers could no longer accept it.
If they can't accept it anymore, the evidence weakened the theory. The answer is undermined. Confirmed is the exact opposite.
Let's try an SAT style question. The architect's plan was blank. Every part had been tested. Choices: noisy, sound, loud, or silent.
The clue is, every part had been tested. My word is solid. The answer is sound, meaning sensible and reliable, not a noise.
Trap alert. Common words can have unusual meanings. Use the meaning the clue supports, not the one you hear most.
Your turn. Pause the video. The play served a blank purpose. It criticized one thing and showed an alternative. Say your own word first.
The clue after the colon names two jobs. My word is two part. The answer is twofold. External sounds smart, but nothing in the text is about outside.
Remember three things. Cover the choices and find the clue. Say your own simple word. And don't pick a word just because it sounds advanced. Great work.
